charts.title: Net Income Attributable to Shareholders
charts.annotation: FY2023 trough ($5.2m) is Cyclone Gabrielle. FY2025 spike ($101.0m) is ~62% underlying earnings + ~38% one-off IFRS 3 gains from consolidating Fayman/ANZ Exports JVs on obtaining control — Underlying NPATAS was $61.8m. NCI (minority shareholders) took a further $19-20m+ of group profit on top of what is shown here.

charts.title: Operating Cash Flow vs Free Cash Flow
charts.annotation: H1 operating and free cash flow are structurally negative every year — working capital builds ahead of the apple harvest (inventory, receivables) and unwinds in H2 as fruit is sold. Not a distress signal; log scale is disabled on this chart because both series cross zero.

charts.title: EBITDA Margin: Reported vs Underlying (FY2025)
charts.annotation: Reported FY2025 EBITDA was $169.9m (18.9% margin shown here); management's Underlying EBITDA, which excludes one-off items, was $137.6m (15.3% margin) — the gap is the same one-off gains distorting NetIncome.

revenue.title: Revenue & YoY Growth
revenue.content:
Total Group revenue across Global Proteins, Horticulture and Logistics.

For Scales: revenue jumped from $584.6m (FY2024) to $899.9m (FY2025, +54%) and then $762.1m in H1-2026 alone (+105% YoY). This is almost entirely the Sep-2025 consolidation of previously part-owned Global Proteins joint ventures (Fayman International/ANZ Exports, Meateor Australia) plus Esro Petfood coming under accounting control in Jun-2026 — not organic volume or price growth. Do not extrapolate these growth rates.

What to watch:

  • Whether growth continues once the acquired businesses lap their first full year (organic growth is guided at only 4-4.5%)
  • The mix shift toward lower-margin Edible Proteins trading revenue diluting group profitability even as the top line grows

revMargin.title: Revenue vs Gross Margin
revMargin.content:
Revenue paired with gross margin (gross profit / revenue) on the secondary axis — the single most informative chart on this business.

For Scales: gross margin fell from 31.3% (H1-2025) to 18.9% (H1-2026) in the very half that revenue nearly doubled. The acquired Edible Proteins/petfood-ingredient trading businesses (Fayman, ANZ Exports) run single-digit EBITDA margins on high revenue, so the group is now bigger but structurally lower-margin than before the 2025 acquisitions.

What to watch:

  • Whether margin stabilises around 18-20% or continues to dilute as more trading volume is added
  • Horticulture's offsetting Premium apple variety mix shift (79% of FY2026 volume targeted vs 74% FY2025), which pulls margin the other way

ebitdaMargin.title: EBITDA Margin (Reported)
ebitdaMargin.content:
Reported EBITDA as a percentage of revenue, each period.

For Scales: this uses reported EBITDA, which for FY2025 includes one-off step-acquisition remeasurement gains booked in Other income. Management's Underlying EBITDA margin (excluding those one-offs) was 15.3% in FY2025, below the reported 18.9% shown here.

What to watch:

  • The trend is more informative than any single period's absolute level given the one-off noise
  • Compare against the Reported vs Underlying chart for the FY2025 gap explicitly

opMargin.title: Operating Margin
opMargin.content:
Operating income (EBIT before significant items, as reported) divided by revenue.

For Scales: operating margin troughed at 6.1% in FY2023 (Cyclone Gabrielle damage to Mr Apple orchards) and has since recovered, though the FY2025-26 acquisition-driven revenue mix keeps it structurally lower than the pre-2025 mid-teens level despite higher absolute dollars.

What to watch:

  • Recovery trajectory versus the pre-cyclone ~15% baseline
  • Whether the Global Proteins FY27 $85m EBITDA target lifts the margin back up as trading-volume dilution is absorbed

netIncome.title: Net Income Attributable to Shareholders
netIncome.content:
Profit after tax and after non-controlling interests (NCI) — the shareholders' share only.

For Scales: group profit is materially larger than what shareholders receive: FY2024 NCI alone took $19.3m of $50.0m group profit (minority partners in Shelby JV LLC, ANZ Exports, Fayman NZ). Do not reconcile this series against headline 'Group profit' figures in filings — they will not match. Separately, FY2025's $100.988m includes ~$26.4m of non-cash, one-off IFRS 3 gains; Underlying NPATAS was $61.8m.

What to watch:

  • The FY2023 Cyclone Gabrielle trough ($5.235m, from $19.4m FY2022) as proof Horticulture earnings can be severely hit by a single weather event
  • Compare against Underlying NPATAS (in the KPI cards) rather than this reported series for a repeatable run-rate

fcf.title: Operating Cash Flow vs Free Cash Flow
fcf.content:
Cash generated by operations, and after capital expenditure.

For Scales: H1 operating and free cash flow are negative in every single year shown — this is structural, not a warning sign. Mr Apple's harvest and export cycle runs through the second half of the calendar year, so working capital (inventory, receivables) builds through H1 ahead of the crop being picked, packed and sold, then unwinds as cash in H2. Never compare an H1 cash-flow figure against a full FY figure as if they were equivalent periods.

What to watch:

  • Full-year (FY) free cash flow is the number that matters for capital allocation and dividends, not any single half
  • FY2024's unusually large capex (-$54.4m) reflects the Bostock orchard acquisition and integration spend
  • Log scale is not offered on this chart because both series cross zero every H1

marginQuality.title: Reported vs Underlying EBITDA Margin (FY2025)
marginQuality.content:
Illustrates the gap between reported and management's Underlying EBITDA for FY2025, the year most distorted by one-off acquisition-accounting items.

For Scales: reported FY2025 EBITDA was $169.9m; Underlying EBITDA (excluding one-off items, mainly the IFRS 3 step-acquisition remeasurement gains) was $137.6m. The DCF valuation is anchored entirely to the Underlying figure and to FY2026 guidance built from it — never to the reported number.

What to watch:

  • Whether FY2026 has any comparable one-off items (none flagged as at the H1-2026 result, aside from the Esro loan impairment which reduces reported, not Underlying, NPATAS)

debt.title: Total Debt vs Cash
debt.content:
Gross borrowings and cash on the balance sheet, each period.

For Scales: the company moved from net cash of $12.5m (FY2024) to net debt of $84.1m (FY2025) to a seasonal peak of $106.7m (H1-2026), funding roughly AUD 91m of Australian Global Proteins acquisitions plus USD 24.4m for the Shelby JV step-up. Leverage remains moderate (~0.7x net debt/EBITDA) and term facilities were extended to July 2029 in August 2026, but the trajectory is upward and deferred acquisition consideration (~$36.7m NZD-equivalent) adds further fixed obligations to FY2030.

What to watch:

  • Whether H2 seasonal working-capital unwind brings net debt back down as management expects
  • Any further debt-funded M&A given management continues to describe an active acquisition pipeline

equity.title: Shareholders' Equity
equity.content:
Book value of equity attributable to Scales shareholders (excludes NCI equity).

For Scales: equity grew only modestly (5yr CAGR ~3.5%) despite revenue and EBITDA growing much faster, because the 50-75% dividend payout policy returns most underlying earnings to shareholders rather than retaining them, and because NCI equity (minority partners' share) sits outside this line.

What to watch:

  • The residual-income cross-check in the DCF uses this line: warranted P/B of ~1.24x book (~NZ$3.83/share) versus the market's ~2.3x

dps.title: Dividend per Share
dps.content:
Ordinary dividends declared per share, each period.

For Scales: policy is to pay out 50-75% of Underlying NPATAS, split roughly evenly between interim and final. FY2025 dividends totalled 25.0 cents per share (12.5 cps interim, 12.5 cps final, partially imputed), up from 15.0 cps in FY2024, and a Dividend Reinvestment Plan (DRP) drew $5.0m of reinvestment on the FY2025 final payment.

What to watch:

  • Whether the FY2026 dividend keeps pace with the raised $55-60m Underlying NPATAS guidance, or whether management retains more cash given rising net debt

shares.title: Shares Outstanding
shares.content:
Total ordinary shares on issue at each period end.

For Scales: the share count has been essentially flat for a decade (~139.8m in FY2016 to ~144.8m in H1-2026), growing only via small dividend-reinvestment-plan issuance rather than dilutive capital raises — a favourable contrast with peers that have funded growth through equity issuance. The DCF holds the share count flat given SBC is immaterial (~0.1% of revenue) and fully expensed in the flows.

What to watch:

  • Any change to this trend if the acquisition-funded growth strategy eventually requires equity rather than debt

dcf.growth_hint: Year-1 revenue growth is acquisition consolidation (~55.6%), not organic; organic growth thereafter is 4.5% fading to 2.5%
